failures.effect: Same Euler blade work but less becomes useful pressure rise: compressor exit pressure falls for the same speed, and EGT rises for the same fuel flow/speed as the governor works to hold N under load.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 isentropic efficiency loss fraction
failures.name: APU core compressor erosion

failures.effect: Less shaft work extracted per unit expansion: more of the gas's enthalpy survives to the exit (higher EGT) and the governor must burn more fuel to hold governed N under the same load.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 isentropic efficiency loss fraction
failures.name: APU turbine damage

failures.effect: Lower delivered bleed pressure for the same demand and spool speed.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 isentropic efficiency loss fraction
failures.name: APU load/bleed compressor erosion

failures.effect: Vanes freeze at their current opening; if that is closed relative to current demand, bleed delivery is starved even though the aircraft calls for more.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 seizure fraction (0=free .. 1=frozen wherever it currently is)
failures.name: APU load compressor IGV actuator jam

failures.effect: Cannot open to recirculate flow when bleed demand drops faster than it can follow: the load compressor's operating point falls below its surge line and it genuinely surges (compressor_map.rs::Point.in_surge).
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 seizure fraction (freezes at whatever recirculation position it held, i.e. stuck open or stuck closed depending on demand history at the moment it jams)
failures.name: APU surge control valve actuator jam

failures.effect: More current for less torque at the same speed: a slower, weaker start, and in severe cases the core never reaches light-off speed.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1, weakens the shared back-EMF/torque constant (STARTER_KE_KT)
failures.name: APU starter motor degradation/failure

failures.effect: At full failure the threshold sits at/above self-sustaining speed, unreachable by the starter alone: a hung start with fuel never lit.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1, raises the effective light-off speed threshold
failures.name: APU igniter failure

failures.effect: Fuel flow freezes at whatever it was delivering; over- or under-fuels the combustor from then on regardless of the governor's command.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 seizure fraction
failures.name: APU fuel control unit (metering valve) fault

failures.effect: A single channel's bias is masked by the other, still-valid channel's own vote/average (ecb.rs::Ecb::step) -- only when both channels are biased the same way, or both fail outright (its own separate 'dual channel speed loss' condition), does the governor see a wrong or missing speed and either overfuel toward overspeed or lose control entirely.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 bias (under-reads true N by up to params::N_SENSOR_MAX_BIAS_PERCENT), or an outright failed=true dropout
failures.name: APU ECB channel A/B speed pickup fault

failures.effect: Tank level falls; the pump progressively starves as level drops below the low-level threshold, pressure falls, and sustained low pressure while running trips low oil pressure protection.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 fraction of MAX_LEAK_RATE_L_S
failures.name: APU oil leak

failures.effect: Door fails to reach fully open, imposing a continuing inlet total-pressure loss that reduces available power and raises EGT for the same demand.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1 seizure fraction
failures.name: APU inlet door actuator jam

failures.effect: More shaft power needed for the same electrical output, loading the core's torque balance.
failures.name: APU generator 1 winding/bearing wear

failures.effect: Removes the normal clamp at rated shaft power: an overloaded generator keeps demanding ever more shaft torque instead of being current-limited.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: boolean, represented as 0/1
failures.name: APU generator 1 overload protection failure

failures.effect: More shaft power needed for the same electrical output, loading the core's torque balance.
failures.name: APU generator 2 winding/bearing wear

failures.effect: Removes the normal clamp at rated shaft power: an overloaded generator keeps demanding ever more shaft torque instead of being current-limited.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: boolean, represented as 0/1
failures.name: APU generator 2 overload protection failure

failures.effect: Cockpit-indicated EGT reads low relative to the true turbine-exit temperature, masking a real overtemperature from the crew/ECAM; the true physics and the hard protective trip are unaffected.
failures.magnitudeMeaning: 0..1, under-reads true EGT by up to params::EGT_SENSOR_MAX_BIAS_C, or an outright dropout
failures.name: APU ECB channel A/B EGT thermocouple fault

failures.effect: A real fire is never confirmed: automatic fuel/bleed shutoff never commands and the bottle cannot be commanded to discharge.
failures.name: APU fire loop failure

failures.effect: Fire is confirmed and shutoff still commands, but the extinguisher bottle never discharges.
failures.name: APU fire bottle squib failure

failures.magnitudeMeaning: Same as fault 1

failures.effect: Same as fault 21, far more severely
failures.magnitudeMeaning: Same as fault 2
failures.name: Engine start duct rupture

failures.effect: Same as fault 3
failures.magnitudeMeaning: Same as fault 3
failures.name: Engine start duct insulation damage

failures.effect: Once that engine lights and its own pressure exceeds the manifold's, a failed check valve lets it push pressure/heat backward into the manifold instead of being blocked -- disturbs every other consumer sharing the manifold during that engine's start

failures.effect: Reduces reservoir air pressurisation, raising cavitation risk for that hydraulic system's pumps at high demand

failures.effect: Same as fault 25, far more severely
failures.magnitudeMeaning: Same as fault 2

failures.effect: Same as fault 3
failures.magnitudeMeaning: Same as fault 3
failures.name: Hydraulic reservoir pressurisation duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Same Euler blade work but less becomes useful pressure rise: compressor exit pressure falls for the same speed, and EGT rises for the same fuel flow/speed as the governor works to hold N under load. Magnitude: 0..1 isentropic efficiency loss fraction.
failures.name: APU core compressor erosion

failures.cause: Less shaft work extracted per unit expansion: more of the gas's enthalpy survives to the exit (higher EGT) and the governor must burn more fuel to hold governed N under the same load. Magnitude: 0..1 isentropic efficiency loss fraction.
failures.name: APU turbine damage

failures.cause: Lower delivered bleed pressure for the same demand and spool speed. Magnitude: 0..1 isentropic efficiency loss fraction.
failures.name: APU load/bleed compressor erosion

failures.cause: Vanes freeze at their current opening; if that is closed relative to current demand, bleed delivery is starved even though the aircraft calls for more. Magnitude: 0..1 seizure fraction (0=free .. 1=frozen wherever it currently is).
failures.name: APU load compressor IGV actuator jam

failures.cause: Cannot open to recirculate flow when bleed demand drops faster than it can follow: the load compressor's operating point falls below its surge line and it genuinely surges (compressor_map.rs::Point.in_surge). Magnitude: 0..1 seizure fraction (freezes at whatever recirculation position it held, i.e. stuck open or stuck closed depending on demand history at the moment it jams).
failures.name: APU surge control valve actuator jam

failures.cause: More current for less torque at the same speed: a slower, weaker start, and in severe cases the core never reaches light-off speed. Magnitude: 0..1, weakens the shared back-EMF/torque constant (STARTER_KE_KT).
failures.name: APU starter motor degradation/failure

failures.cause: At full failure the threshold sits at/above self-sustaining speed, unreachable by the starter alone: a hung start with fuel never lit. Magnitude: 0..1, raises the effective light-off speed threshold.
failures.name: APU igniter failure

failures.cause: Fuel flow freezes at whatever it was delivering; over- or under-fuels the combustor from then on regardless of the governor's command. Magnitude: 0..1 seizure fraction.
failures.name: APU fuel control unit (metering valve) fault

failures.cause: A single channel's bias is masked by the other, still-valid channel's own vote/average (ecb.rs::Ecb::step) -- only when both channels are biased the same way, or both fail outright (its own separate 'dual channel speed loss' condition), does the governor see a wrong or missing speed and either overfuel toward overspeed or lose control entirely. Magnitude: 0..1 bias (under-reads true N by up to params::N_SENSOR_MAX_BIAS_PERCENT), or an outright failed=true dropout.
failures.name: APU ECB channel A/B speed pickup fault

failures.cause: Tank level falls; the pump progressively starves as level drops below the low-level threshold, pressure falls, and sustained low pressure while running trips low oil pressure protection. Magnitude: 0..1 fraction of MAX_LEAK_RATE_L_S.
failures.name: APU oil leak

failures.cause: Door fails to reach fully open, imposing a continuing inlet total-pressure loss that reduces available power and raises EGT for the same demand. Magnitude: 0..1 seizure fraction.
failures.name: APU inlet door actuator jam

failures.cause: More shaft power needed for the same electrical output, loading the core's torque balance. Magnitude: 0..1.
failures.name: APU generator 1 winding/bearing wear

failures.cause: Removes the normal clamp at rated shaft power: an overloaded generator keeps demanding ever more shaft torque instead of being current-limited. Magnitude: boolean, represented as 0/1.
failures.name: APU generator 1 overload protection failure

failures.cause: More shaft power needed for the same electrical output, loading the core's torque balance. Magnitude: 0..1.
failures.name: APU generator 2 winding/bearing wear

failures.cause: Removes the normal clamp at rated shaft power: an overloaded generator keeps demanding ever more shaft torque instead of being current-limited. Magnitude: boolean, represented as 0/1.
failures.name: APU generator 2 overload protection failure

failures.cause: Cockpit-indicated EGT reads low relative to the true turbine-exit temperature, masking a real overtemperature from the crew/ECAM; the true physics and the hard protective trip are unaffected. Magnitude: 0..1, under-reads true EGT by up to params::EGT_SENSOR_MAX_BIAS_C, or an outright dropout.
failures.name: APU ECB channel A/B EGT thermocouple fault

failures.cause: A real fire is never confirmed: automatic fuel/bleed shutoff never commands and the bottle cannot be commanded to discharge. Magnitude: 0..1.
failures.name: APU fire loop failure

failures.cause: Fire is confirmed and shutoff still commands, but the extinguisher bottle never discharges. Magnitude: 0..1.
failures.name: APU fire bottle squib failure

failures.cause: reduced core flow capacity, raised backpressure, surge-margin loss Magnitude: deposited molten-ash mass / GENERIC 2 kg full-blockage reference.
failures.name: Volcanic ash NGV glassing

failures.cause: permanent compressor efficiency loss Magnitude: GENERIC erosion-rate integral of unmelted ash flux x velocity^2.5, capped 0.25.
failures.name: Volcanic ash compressor erosion

failures.cause: fan damage, permanent compressor efficiency loss, elevated flameout/roll-back risk especially at low power Magnitude: fan: cumulative energy density / reference; compressor: GENERIC erosion per kg ingested, capped 0.25; flameout: ingested mass / a GENERIC tolerance that shrinks with N1 (CS-E 790 / 14 CFR 33.68).
failures.name: Hail/ice engine ingestion

failures.cause: Heats that wing's leading-edge zone directly (real risk: an undetected WAI duct leak burning through the leading-edge structure, the well-publicised reason this class of system carries ODLS at all) Magnitude: Same as fault 1.
failures.name: Wing anti-ice duct leak

failures.cause: Same as fault 1, far more severely; reliably trips that side's leading-edge ODLS Magnitude: Same as fault 2.
failures.name: Wing anti-ice duct rupture

failures.cause: Same as fault 3 Magnitude: Same as fault 3.
failures.name: Wing anti-ice duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Mass flow escapes to the pylon zone (leak.rs::step); manifold/downstream pressure sags proportionally, and the pylon ODLS eventually trips on the resulting heat if severe enough Magnitude: Crack area, 0 healthy .. 1 = 2% of the duct's bore area (leak.rs::LEAK_AREA_FRACTION_OF_BORE).
failures.name: Engine bleed duct leak

failures.cause: Large mass flow escapes as a near-sonic jet; above leak.rs::RUPTURE_JET_ONSET the jet is treated as impinging (higher heat-transfer effectiveness into the pylon zone), reliably tripping that pylon's ODLS and, once confirmed, latching that engine's isolation valve shut (network.rs) Magnitude: Severance area, 0 healthy .. 1 = full duct bore area.
failures.name: Engine bleed duct rupture

failures.cause: The pylon zone receives ordinary (non-fault) duct heat loss at up to 10x the healthy rate -- no ODLS trip on its own at normal bleed temperatures, but raises the pylon's baseline temperature so a subsequent leak trips ODLS sooner Magnitude: Lagging condition, 0 intact .. 1 fully bare pipe (duct.rs::DuctSection::BARE_PIPE_MULTIPLIER = 10x conductance).
failures.name: Engine bleed duct insulation damage

failures.cause: For the same cooling flow the outlet runs hotter (precooler.rs's NTU-effectiveness heat exchange); the FAV opens further to compensate, and at full fouling may not hold the outlet near target at all, raising overtemperature-trip risk Magnitude: Conductance loss fraction, 0 clean .. 1 (precooler.rs::FOULING_MAX_REDUCTION = 80% loss at 1.0).
failures.name: Engine precooler fouling

failures.cause: No further cooling-flow modulation: stuck closed (or partly open) leaves the bleed hot regardless of demand; the hard overtemperature protection (true-temperature-based, module docs) is unaffected by this fault and can still force full flow via a separate path -- but a valve seized fully open cannot heed it either Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 seized at its position when the fault engaged.
failures.name: Engine precooler fan air valve stuck

failures.cause: The modulating FAV loop under/over-corrects against a stale reading; the independent hard overtemperature trip still sees the true temperature (precooler.rs module docs: a biased sensor cannot defeat it), so this fault degrades regulation quality without defeating the safety protection Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 frozen at the last good reading.
failures.name: Engine precooler outlet temperature sensor fault

failures.cause: When duct pressure sags below ambient (e.g. low power, other faults), outside air is drawn back into the duct uncontrolled instead of being blocked, cooling/diluting it unpredictably Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 fully open in reverse.
failures.name: Engine precooler check valve failure

failures.cause: Same as fault 1; heats the APU bay instead of a pylon Magnitude: Same as fault 1, applied to the APU bay zone.
failures.name: APU bleed duct leak

failures.cause: Same as fault 2; can trip the APU bay ODLS and latch the APU isolation valve shut Magnitude: Same as fault 2, applied to the APU bay zone.
failures.name: APU bleed duct rupture

failures.cause: Same as fault 3, applied to the APU bay zone Magnitude: Same as fault 3.
failures.name: APU bleed duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Same as fault 4 Magnitude: Same as fault 4.
failures.name: APU precooler fouling

failures.cause: Same as fault 5 Magnitude: Same as fault 5.
failures.name: APU precooler fan air valve stuck

failures.cause: Same as fault 6 Magnitude: Same as fault 6.
failures.name: APU precooler outlet temperature sensor fault

failures.cause: Same as fault 7 Magnitude: Same as fault 7.
failures.name: APU precooler check valve failure

failures.cause: Stuck shut: no HP6 backup once IP8 falls below the EASA switch-over pressure, engine duct pressure sags. Stuck open: continues drawing hot HP6 air even once IP8 alone would suffice, an avoidable EGT/performance penalty upstream at the compressor. Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 seized at whatever position it last held.
failures.name: Engine HP valve stuck

failures.cause: Stuck shut: that engine can no longer supply its own duct at all (a real 'ENG n BLEED FAULT'), leaving it dependent on cross-bleed. Stuck open: an ODLS trip's own isolation command can no longer close it, defeating the real isolation this system exists for. Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 seized at whatever position it last held.
failures.name: Engine PR (shutoff) valve stuck

failures.cause: The passive IP8 tap can no longer pass its normal share of flow, forcing the HP valve to open further/more often than normal to hold regulation -- a real, measurable shift from the efficient IP8 source to the costlier HP6 one. Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 fully stuck shut.
failures.name: Engine IP8 check valve stuck closed

failures.cause: Starves that pack of supply pressure; the manifold and other consumers are largely unaffected (downstream of the pack valve) Magnitude: Same as fault 1.
failures.name: Pack supply duct leak

failures.cause: Same as fault 18, far more severely Magnitude: Same as fault 2.
failures.name: Pack supply duct rupture

failures.cause: Same as fault 3, applied to the wing-root zone Magnitude: Same as fault 3.
failures.name: Pack supply duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Weakens starter torque available at the engine during a pneumatic start; heats that engine's own pylon zone Magnitude: Same as fault 1.
failures.name: Engine start duct leak

failures.cause: Same as fault 21, far more severely Magnitude: Same as fault 2.
failures.name: Engine start duct rupture

failures.cause: Same as fault 3 Magnitude: Same as fault 3.
failures.name: Engine start duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Once that engine lights and its own pressure exceeds the manifold's, a failed check valve lets it push pressure/heat backward into the manifold instead of being blocked -- disturbs every other consumer sharing the manifold during that engine's start Magnitude: 0 healthy (perfect non-return) .. 1 fully open in reverse.
failures.name: Engine start duct check valve failure

failures.cause: Reduces reservoir air pressurisation, raising cavitation risk for that hydraulic system's pumps at high demand Magnitude: Same as fault 1.
failures.name: Hydraulic reservoir pressurisation duct leak

failures.cause: Same as fault 25, far more severely Magnitude: Same as fault 2.
failures.name: Hydraulic reservoir pressurisation duct rupture

failures.cause: Same as fault 3 Magnitude: Same as fault 3.
failures.name: Hydraulic reservoir pressurisation duct insulation damage

failures.cause: Loop A stops providing a valid reading; loop B alone still governs trip/no-trip (fail-safe voting, odls.rs). Both loops open at once reports a FAULT with no valid detection at all Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 open (>= 0.5 treated as fully open, odls.rs::interpret).
failures.name: ODLS loop A open circuit

failures.cause: Loop A pegs at a fixed reading well past the trip threshold, tripping that zone's isolation on its own (a real false alarm from a genuine wiring fault, distinct from fault 32) Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 shorted (>= 0.5 treated as fully shorted).
failures.name: ODLS loop A short circuit

failures.cause: Same as fault 28, loop B Magnitude: Same as fault 28, loop B.
failures.name: ODLS loop B open circuit

failures.cause: Same as fault 29, loop B Magnitude: Same as fault 29, loop B.
failures.name: ODLS loop B short circuit

failures.cause: Trips and latches that zone's isolation valve shut with no real overheat present -- a nuisance trip, not a wiring fault on either specific loop (distinct from faults 29/31) Magnitude: 0 healthy .. 1 = a cold zone trips on its own regardless of real temperature (odls.rs::FALSE_DETECTION_FULL_K).
failures.name: ODLS false detection

failures.cause: forward transfers (inner/mid/outer to feed, forward trim path) are throttled exactly as `cg_transfer::achieved_transfer_rate_kg_s` models, and the diverted fuel is an unmetered loss `leak::LeakDetector` can catch Magnitude: 0..1 diverted fraction.
failures.name: Forward transfer gallery leak

failures.cause: aft transfers and the jettison feed path through AftGalleryJunction1/2 are throttled and the diverted fuel is an unmetered loss Magnitude: 0..1 diverted fraction.
failures.name: Aft transfer gallery leak

failures.cause: oxygen escapes through a choked orifice, so indicated bottle pressure falls steadily and the temperature-corrected reading falls with it; at full magnitude the group is empty in about twenty minutes and the low-pressure caution comes up on the way Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of a 1 mm^2 equivalent orifice (not a 0..1 loss fraction).
failures.name: Crew oxygen cylinder leak

failures.cause: above about 0.34 the disc ruptures at or below the cylinder's own charge pressure and dumps the whole group overboard through its 3 mm bore in under a minute; below that it still ruptures early if the bay heats the bottle, which is the case it exists for Magnitude: 0 .. 1 reduction of the 2775 psig rupture pressure.
failures.name: Crew oxygen overpressure disc degraded

failures.cause: at full magnitude the low-pressure distribution falls to zero and the mask regulators stop delivering altogether, while the bottle stays full -- the quantity gauge cannot see this one Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of the valve's travel lost; the supply only starves in the last few percent, because a partly open shutoff valve still passes far more than this system draws.
failures.name: Crew oxygen supply valve seized

failures.cause: distribution pressure falls below what a demand regulator needs to open; past about half setpoint the masks deliver nothing at all rather than delivering something thin Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of the setpoint lost, so 1 delivers nothing.
failures.name: Crew oxygen reducer setting low

failures.cause: distribution pressure rises until the low-pressure relief lifts at 1.5 times setpoint and holds it there, venting the excess overboard Magnitude: 0 .. 1 added to the setpoint, so 1 doubles it.
failures.name: Crew oxygen reducer setting high

failures.cause: cylinder pressure bleeds continuously into the low-pressure side and out through its relief with nobody breathing any of it; a full group empties overnight, so the signature is a bottle that was full yesterday and is not today Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of a 0.01 mm^2 equivalent orifice past the poppet.
failures.name: Crew oxygen reducer seat leak

failures.cause: the low-pressure side leaks to the flight deck whether or not a mask is donned, draining the cylinder over about five hours at full magnitude Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of a 0.5 mm^2 equivalent orifice at 85 psi.
failures.name: Crew oxygen distribution or mask hose leak

failures.cause: station 1's delivered oxygen fraction falls from the alveolar-solved schedule toward 0.2095 -- the mask breathes normally and contains cabin air, so it is silent at altitude, and the bottle stops being drawn down, which is why the quantity gauge cannot catch it either Magnitude: 0 .. 1, how far the diluter is jammed toward its cabin-air inlet.
failures.name: Crew mask 1 diluter jammed to ambient

failures.cause: station 2's delivered oxygen fraction falls from the alveolar-solved schedule toward 0.2095 -- the mask breathes normally and contains cabin air, so it is silent at altitude, and the bottle stops being drawn down, which is why the quantity gauge cannot catch it either Magnitude: 0 .. 1, how far the diluter is jammed toward its cabin-air inlet.
failures.name: Crew mask 2 diluter jammed to ambient

failures.cause: station 3's delivered oxygen fraction falls from the alveolar-solved schedule toward 0.2095 -- the mask breathes normally and contains cabin air, so it is silent at altitude, and the bottle stops being drawn down, which is why the quantity gauge cannot catch it either Magnitude: 0 .. 1, how far the diluter is jammed toward its cabin-air inlet.
failures.name: Crew mask 3 diluter jammed to ambient

failures.cause: station 4's delivered oxygen fraction falls from the alveolar-solved schedule toward 0.2095 -- the mask breathes normally and contains cabin air, so it is silent at altitude, and the bottle stops being drawn down, which is why the quantity gauge cannot catch it either Magnitude: 0 .. 1, how far the diluter is jammed toward its cabin-air inlet.
failures.name: Crew mask 4 diluter jammed to ambient

failures.cause: the masks still present -- that is the latch's job -- and that fraction of them delivers nothing when pulled; cabin oxygen flow and the generators' heat both fall in proportion, and the unfired generators are still full Magnitude: 0 .. 1, the fraction of units that will not light.
failures.name: Passenger oxygen generator initiators dud

failures.cause: the burn stops early, so the cabin's oxygen stops before the rated 15 minutes are up and unburnt candle is left behind; at 0.5 the supply runs out after about seven and a half minutes Magnitude: 0 .. 1, the fraction of the candle the front fails to reach.
failures.name: Passenger oxygen candle quenches early

failures.cause: those units burn inside a closed PSU with no masks presented, reaching a case temperature near 300 C and putting their full chemical heat into the cabin zone until the candle is gone; the supply they represent is spent and cannot be recovered in flight Magnitude: 0 .. 1, the fraction of units that light unbidden.
failures.name: Passenger oxygen generator inadvertent ignition

failures.cause: that fraction of the cabin gets no mask at all when the system deploys, so no generator in it is ever lit; the deployed fraction, the oxygen flow and the generator heat all fall together Magnitude: 0 .. 1, the fraction of PSU doors that stay shut.
failures.name: Passenger oxygen PSU latches seized

failures.cause: at full magnitude the cabin altitude trigger never presents the masks, however high the cabin goes; the flight deck's manual command is a separate path and still works, which is exactly why it is there Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of the automatic deployment authority lost.
failures.name: Passenger oxygen automatic deployment controller failed

failures.cause: indicated first-aid bottle pressure falls steadily; once it drops below about half the 50 psi delivery setting the outlets stop flowing entirely, and the cabin has no therapeutic oxygen at all Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of a 1 mm^2 equivalent orifice.
failures.name: First-aid oxygen cylinder leak

failures.cause: past about a third the disc ruptures at the cylinder's own charge pressure and dumps it overboard in well under a minute Magnitude: 0 .. 1 reduction of the 2700 psig rupture pressure.
failures.name: First-aid oxygen overpressure disc degraded

failures.cause: delivery pressure falls; below half setting the continuous-flow outlets stop delivering, with the bottle still full Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of the 50 psi setting lost.
failures.name: First-aid oxygen regulator setting low

failures.cause: the cylinder bleeds down over hours into the low-pressure side with nobody using it, so the bottle is found short at the next check Magnitude: 0 .. 1 of a 0.01 mm^2 equivalent orifice past the poppet.
failures.name: First-aid oxygen regulator seat leak

failures.cause: a continuous-flow outlet does not care whether anyone is breathing through it, so each stuck outlet drains the cylinder at its full 4 L/min and the supply is gone long before it is wanted Magnitude: 0 .. 1, the fraction of the installed outlets flowing unattended.
failures.name: First-aid oxygen outlet stuck open
